rule.description: AI-capable process initiated a network connection
rule.info: Detects outbound Sysmon network events from common AI tools, coding agents, local LLM tools, and package/runtime launchers often used to start AI tooling.
Falsepositives: Developer tools such as node.exe and python.exe are common. Use child rules and environment allowlists to tune severity.

rule.description: Whitelist Interaction: AI-capable process loopback network connection
AI tool connected to public AI or model hosting endpoint
rule.info: Detects AI-capable processes connecting to common public AI APIs, chat endpoints, model providers, or model hosting domains.
Falsepositives: Approved AI workflows and model downloads. Validate user, host, repository, and business justification.

rule.description: AI coding agent connected to an external network destination
rule.info: Detects coding agents or agentic IDE tools initiating external network connections.
Falsepositives: Normal product updates, extension sync, and approved AI service use.

rule.description: Local AI or LLM tool connected to an external network destination
rule.info: Detects local LLM applications initiating external network connections, often for model downloads, telemetry, updates, or remote APIs.
Falsepositives: Approved model downloads and update checks.

rule.description: Script runtime connected to AI or model hosting endpoint
rule.info: Detects generic runtimes commonly used by AI tools or MCP servers when they connect to public AI endpoints.
Falsepositives: Approved development scripts using AI APIs.

rule.description: AI-capable process connected to private network destination
rule.info: Detects AI tools and agent runtimes connecting to private network destinations, which can indicate local MCP servers, internal proxies, gateways, or internal services.
Falsepositives: Approved internal package mirrors, update caches, or local AI gateways.
